investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state within the eval timeout window.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. Only 2 of 6 nodes carry this resource, and both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time. The remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck unschedulable for 134–144 seconds before the eval timed out, and no VM identity or state was ever returned. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state within the eval timeout window.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. Only 2 of 6 nodes carry this resource, and both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time. The remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck unschedulable for 134–144 seconds before the eval timed out, and no VM identity or state was ever returned. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message). No preemption victims were available, so the pod could not be force-scheduled.

SECONDARY — Node affinity or selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving only 2 nodes eligible. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or if nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or relabeled, the effective scheduling pool may have shrunk below what is needed to absorb concurrent remote-agent pods.

TERTIARY — Concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if other remote-agent pods (from users or other eval runs) were already running on the 2 eligible nodes, the resource slots may have been fully occupied at the time of the eval, causing a transient exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity ceiling.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-08 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, no remote agent VM was ever provisioned, and the runtime eval never received any response evidence — leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and "No preemption victims found" confirms that no capacity was available and preemption could not free any. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the peer-pod VM resource type, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the agent pod never started, the probe in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918, createAgent call) never completed, and zero evidence was returned against the contract defined in check-expectations.json lines 266–270.
